assumptions: TaskState counts one submitted Task; a newly constructed continuation is a distinct task token.
Rust Option::take, Arc::try_unwrap, mutex exclusion and unique mutable Future polling implement the modeled custody transfers; the Rust language semantics are not encoded in Lean.
A recovered rejection is the branch where the host wrapper has been dropped; retained or already-polled wrappers stay owned by the host.
Cleanup starts with the LIFO sequence delivered by the existing Effects.claim model. Callback outputs, panic conversion and wakeups are environment events.
The theorems prove safety for arbitrary finite traces. Eventual completion additionally requires host polling and eventual callback termination.

evidence_commands.purpose: Runs the real scheduler acceptance/rejection, suspended cleanup recovery and serial asynchronous cleanup integration tests.

assumptions: Callback destruction is serialized with its synchronous poll. Rust declaration-order field destruction drops Admitted.future before Admitted._permit.
Usage.held is a ghost ledger of live Permit objects; a release event consumes an owned permit after its future destructor finishes.
Natural-number bounds are instantiated with the platform usize maximum, configured callback limits and u64 identifiers as applicable.
Lease acquisition uses count.fetch_update and a separate retired.load. The completed-operation lease model does not establish a Rust memory-model linearization proof for those two atomic objects.
Valid ABI cloning holds an existing counted lease through acquisition; descriptor release is uniquely owned and its result is published once.
Tokio abort/drop scheduling, foreign destructors, libloading and operating-system image unmapping remain implementation boundaries.

evidence_commands.purpose: Checks count/byte admission, cancellation during a blocking native poll, and unpolled future destruction order in production types.
Runs real dynamic-library retirement, quiescence and unload-policy scenarios through the native driver.

assumptions: Each Peer models a stable connection identity. The historical allocation frontier is ghost state after recipient reclaim; the concrete Recipient may be removed once that connection is dead.
Entry.batch is the ghost inverse of the pending IDs in live Batch objects. Commit transfers rollback ownership once the Outgoing commit callback executes.

BoundedPeer represents the exact finite domain of the concrete routes HashMap; fresh insertion, filtering and commit preserve its bijective membership and cardinality. The existing export decision receives capacityAvailable computed from keys.length < max_exports. Rust HashMap memory/layout/hash implementation remains external.
Directory mutex mutations are atomic model transitions. Detached references are dropped in a separate step, corresponding to Rust's drop(discarded) outside the lock.
Retirement marking and indexed sweeping are separate events, preserving the interval in which lifetime.finish has executed but the directory lock has not yet been acquired.
Directory-owned Arc references are tracked individually; Arc clones returned to callers, value rewriting, network transmission and remote peer cooperation have separate contracts.

evidence_commands.purpose: Exercises production release, lifetime retirement, batch rollback, both connection ends, every secondary index and destructor execution outside the directory lock.
